html:
In 711 a Muslim army crossed from North Africa into Spain and within about seven years conquered most of the Iberian peninsula from the Visigoths. The land under Muslim rule became al-Andalus.

The commander was Tariq ibn Ziyad, a Berber freedman serving Musa ibn Nusayr, the Umayyad governor of North Africa. He landed at the rock that still carries his name: Gibraltar comes from Jabal Tariq, "Tariq's mountain". His army was small and mostly Berber. The Visigothic kingdom was split by a dispute over the throne, and King Roderic was killed in battle at the Guadalete river in 711. The capital, Toledo, fell soon after. Musa followed with a larger army in 712, and by about 718 nearly all of Iberia was taken.

Only the far northern mountains held out. A small Christian kingdom formed in Asturias after a skirmish at Covadonga around 722; Spanish tradition later treated this as the start of the Reconquista. Raids north of the Pyrenees into Frankish Gaul were turned back at the Battle of Tours in 732.

When the Abbasids overthrew the Umayyads in 750, a surviving prince, Abd al-Rahman, escaped to Spain and set up the Emirate of Cordoba in 756. Muslim rule in some part of Iberia then lasted until 1492.
sum: In 711 a Muslim army crossed from North Africa into Spain and within about seven years conquered most of the Iberian peninsula from the Visigoths. The land under Muslim rule became al-Andalus.
